motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Public Infrastructure District Policy. Councilmember Curtis expressed concern with the risks associated with Public Infrastructure Districts (PIDs), allowing developers to oversee resident taxes, and the potential abuse of inflated reimbursement rates. As he has no intention of applying a PID to a residential development, he would prefer not to have associated standards in Municipal Code. Councilmembers Wright and Love concurred with not approving PIDs for residential developments. Mayor Westmoreland noted the benefit of the additional oversight and risk reduction measures of invested parties. City Attorney Jeremy Cook clarified the reason for placing the item on the agenda was to identify Council concerns to be able to address the issues and establish approval criteria in the governing document. Section 4 provides for the Council to deny a PID for any reason. PIDs could allow for improvements desired in the City that would otherwise be not viable financially. Discussion ensued regarding concerns regarding: • The impact of the cost of the PID on house affordability; Eagle Mountain City Council Meeting – September 20, 2022 Page 11 of 13 • The potential for homebuyers to not understand the higher tax rate when purchasing their home; • The impact on the ability of residents to sell their homes; • The PID cost increasing as the value of the home increases; • Development funding mechanisms; • Placing the burden of improvements and benefits to the overall City on a specific group of residents; and • Details of the bond payments. Councilmember Love requested additional information regarding commercial PIDs. City Administrator Paul Jerome recommended any PIDs approved in the City have an economic development component. He does not foresee a circumstance in which the City would find a residential PID to be beneficial.
motions.motion: Councilmember Love moved to table a resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, adopting the Public Infrastructure Policy inviting staff, if desired, to bring back the item as a commercial economic development policy and tool that excludes residential development. AMENDED MOTION: Councilmember Love moved to table a resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, adopting the Public Infrastructure Policy. Councilmember Curtis seconded the motion.
